statement: Adopted this lane from a dead worktree (agent-a1a094db1eaab36a3, branch lane/x06-5-weaver, never pushed to origin). The dead worker left crates/enforcer-memory/src/{enrichment,queue,summaries}.rs and src/weaver/mod.rs uncommitted plus lib.rs/Cargo.toml wiring edits. Salvage assessment: the code was structurally strong -- correct hot/warm/cold priority queue (queue.rs), bounded-concurrency worker pool with retry/backoff (enrichment.rs), dead-letter queue, and blue/green embedding-version migration hooks (weaver/mod.rs) -- but was unverified WIP that had never been built or tested. Two real defects were found only by actually running it: (1) migration_cutover_never_mixes_generations was a plain #[test] calling Weaver::builder().build(), which internally does tokio::spawn -- this panics with no reactor running outside a tokio runtime; (2) WorkerPool::shutdown deadlocked permanently because the drain loop captures its own WeaverQueueHandle clone for the lifetime of the loop (needed to re-enqueue retries), so the mpsc channel can never observe "all senders dropped" from the outside -- shutdown awaited a JoinHandle that could never resolve.
why: Salvage triage (L38 in the playbook) says a partial worktree gets adopted rather than discarded when the mechanism is right but unverified -- this was exactly that case: sound design, zero verification.
howToApply: Any future salvage-adoption task must budget time to actually RUN the salvaged code (build+test), not just review it by reading -- both defects here were invisible on read-through and only surfaced as a genuine test hang that took significant diagnosis (initially mistaken for shared-machine build contention before isolating to a real deadlock).

statement: A tokio worker-pool drain loop that needs its own WeaverQueueHandle/Sender clone to re-enqueue retries can never terminate by waiting for "all senders dropped" (mpsc channel close), because the loop itself permanently holds one sender. Fixed in enforcer_memory::enrichment::WorkerPool by adding an explicit Arc<tokio::sync::Notify> stop signal: the drain loop races queue.recv_next() against stop.notified() in a biased tokio::select! (task-ready branch first, so in-flight backlog always drains before a pending stop is honored), and WorkerPool::shutdown calls stop.notify_one() instead of relying on channel closure.
why: This is a general pattern hazard for any producer-consumer pool where the consumer loop is also a producer back into its own queue (retry, requeue-on-backpressure, etc.) -- channel-closed-based shutdown silently deadlocks in exactly that shape, and the failure mode (test hangs forever, no panic, no error) is easy to misdiagnose as slow CI/shared-machine contention rather than a logic bug.
howToApply: Any future enforcer-rust worker pool with a self-requeuing drain loop must use an explicit stop signal (Notify, CancellationToken-equivalent, or an atomic flag polled in the select) for shutdown, never bare channel-closed detection, whenever the loop itself holds a sender/handle clone for its own lifetime.

statement: Added crate::enrichment::TaskOutcome (Succeeded/RetryScheduled/DeadLettered) broadcast on an optional tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender threaded through WorkerPoolConfig::on_outcome / WeaverBuilder::with_outcome_channel, so every hard test in tests/weaver_enrichment.rs and the in-module tests in enrichment.rs/weaver/mod.rs synchronize deterministically on a channel receive instead of a tokio::time::sleep poll loop. Also rewrote every test to avoid clippy::expect_used/unwrap_used/panic (workspace-wide deny, including in test code) by giving each async test a -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> signature and using ? -- required a lock_or_msg() helper because std::sync::Mutex's PoisonError embeds the MutexGuard and is not 'static, so it cannot convert into Box<dyn Error> via a bare ?.
why: D-09/IMPLEMENTATION_PACKS §6 explicitly requires the hard tests be deterministic and synchronize via channels/notify, never sleeps -- the salvaged code's original tests all used tokio::time::sleep polling loops (bounded but still nondeterministic/race-prone), and the workspace lint config (Cargo.toml [workspace.lints.clippy]) denies expect_used/unwrap_used/panic crate-wide with zero #[allow] permitted, which the salvaged tests also violated throughout.
howToApply: Any future async test needing deterministic completion-signal synchronization in this crate should reuse the TaskOutcome/on_outcome pattern (or WeaverBuilder::with_outcome_channel for tests going through the public Weaver API) rather than inventing a new signal mechanism or falling back to sleep-polling.

statement: Added tests/fixtures/memory/weaver/{widget_v1.rs,widget_v2.rs} -- two real revisions of the same small Rust symbol, sha256-hashed at test time (crates/enforcer-memory tests already depend on sha2 in [dev-dependencies], added alongside tokio's dev-dependency entry) so tests/weaver_enrichment.rs's file-changed/node-changed hard tests exercise real file content hashes rather than inline synthetic strings, matching tests/code_graph_indexer.rs's established real-fixture-over-literal convention.
why: Consistency with the crate's existing fixture discipline (code_graph_indexer.rs copies a small multi-language fixture repo into a real git working tree rather than hand-writing strings) -- weaver events reference rel_path/content_hash pairs that in production come from real file content, so the hard tests should too.
howToApply: Future weaver-adjacent hard tests needing realistic file content/hashes should extend tests/fixtures/memory/weaver/ rather than inventing inline literals.
